newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans sharply lower in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans sharply lower in volatile trade.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were sharply lower early in volatile trade with old crop down on small-lot selling tied to liquidation of the July and profit taking on bull spreads, pit sources said.

New crop months were also lower hit by forecasts for good crop growing weather. The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook called for above normal rainfall and below normal temperatures in the Midwest from July 15 to July 19.
Traders said volume in the July and August was thin and volatile. Small-lot orders were enough to move the market several cents.

Losses were limited by USDA weekly export sales data. USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans for the week ended July 3 totalled 590,200 tonnes of new crop soy, above expectations for 150,000 to 250,000 tonnes. Sales of old soy totalled 76,400 tonnes, near the high end of expectations for 40,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
In early trade, Iowa Grain sold two million bushels Novemberand Refco Inc sold 1.5 million November.
At 0953 CDT, soybeans were down 12 to 8-3/4 cents per bushel with July off 12 at $7.77.
